lines.en: Chapter two, concerning a thing which is hoped for, whether it will happen or not.

lines.en: Chapter six, concerning lent substance.

lines.text: Caput septimum, de rebus cuiusdam mortui derelictis.
lines.en: Chapter seven, concerning the abandoned things of a certain dead person.

lines.text: Caput octauum, de regno utrum acquiratur.
lines.en: Chapter eight, concerning a kingdom, whether it will be acquired.

lines.text: Caput nonum, quaestio de regno.
lines.en: Chapter nine, a question concerning a kingdom.

lines.en: Chapter ten, an interrogation concerning a kingdom.

lines.text: Caput undecimum, de inueniendo Hylech nati.
lines.en: Chapter eleven, concerning finding the Hyleg of a native.

lines.text: Caput duodecimum, quaestio de regno.
lines.en: Chapter twelve, a question concerning a kingdom.

summary.headline: Māshāʾallāh on Reception
summary.text: Table of contents for Māshāʾallāh’s book on reception, covering hoped-for events, illness, substance, kingdoms, abandoned property, and finding the Hyleg. The opening explains interrogational astrology through the seven planets, twelve houses, exaltations, descensions, conjunctions, separations, and receptions.
